div.head: Quadr Arg 3
div.ab: Communi denique commodo prouidus et saluti, omnem regnorum eius sapientiam, meritorum potius quam personarum estimatione, quanta potuit sollicitudine congregare curauit, memorabilem cum eis synodum, in secula successiua profuturam, Deo grata consideratione diffiniens generaliter ac principaliter in uniuersis, que ad sanctam matrem nostram ecclesiam pertinere uidebantur, secundo loco de statu et agendis regni eius, in opprimendis uitiis et augendis uirtutibus, quicquid diligens sapientum indagatio ualuit perscrutari.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 532 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

Zu Zeile 2 personarum [wo {a} ausgefallen] vgl. Ded. 25
On line 2 personarum [where {a} has dropped out] cf. Ded. 25

div.ab: Provident, then, for the common advantage and welfare, he took care to gather, with as much solicitude as he could, all the wisdom of his kingdoms, by estimation of merits rather than of persons, defining with them, with consideration pleasing to God, a memorable synod, to be of profit to successive ages, generally and principally in all things that seemed to pertain to our holy mother Church, and in the second place concerning the state and affairs of his kingdom, in suppressing vices and increasing virtues, whatever the diligent investigation of wise men was able to search out.
